title: US Futures Mixed After Rally On Wednesday — MU, TSLA, AAPL, MSFT, APP, NVDA, IREN In Focus - Stocktwits
content: U.S. equity futures were mixed early on Thursday after the previous session's rally, helped by a sharp drop in oil prices and greater clarity following Democrats’ midterm victories. As of 3.45 a.m. ET, S&P 500 futures fell 0.11%, while Nasdaq-100 futures declined around 1%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures moved in the opposite direction, gaining 0.5%. The cautious start followed a strong session on Wednesday, when major U.S. indexes closed higher as technology and semiconductor stocks rebounded. The S&P 500 ended 2% higher on Wednesday, while the Nasdaq-100 advanced 1%. The Dow climbed 3% to its highest level in a year. The small-cap Russell 2000 also added 1.6%. Oil prices rebounded in early Thursday trading after initially extending their losses, as investors weighed whether Republicans’ setbacks in this week's congressional elections could lower the risk of further escalation in the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Brent crude futures rose around 1.05% to $95.61 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 0.3% to $88.38 as of 3:45 a.m. ET. The recovery followed a sharp sell-off on Wednesday, when both benchmarks plunged more than 8% to settle at their lowest levels since August 31. Micron Technology (MU): Micron came under pressure in early premarket trading on Thursday, with shares down over 3% as concerns about tighter AI regulation compounded weakness across technology stocks. Democratic Rep. Yassamin Ansari of Arizona called on Wednesday for a pause in advanced AI development until adequate regulations are in place. The prospect of stricter rules has raised concerns that congressional action could slow data center expansion and limit demand for AI computing capacity. Tesla (TSLA): A potential Tesla-SpaceX merger is facing fresh questions as political pressure on Elon Musk adds to concerns about regulatory hurdles and the value of any takeover premium. Mark Tepper, CEO of Strategic Wealth Partners, raised doubts about the prospects of such a deal, stating that greater scrutiny of Musk could create challenges for both companies. His comments followed Democrats' victories in both chambers of Congress and the Texas governor's race. Texas is home to major Tesla and SpaceX operations, as well as their planned Terafab chipmaking project. Tesla shares had dropped 3% on Wednesday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 4%, and were down 2.2% in early premarket trading on Thursday. Apple (AAPL): Apple crossed the $5-trillion valuation mark on Wednesday as its shares climbed to a 52-week high, supported by optimism around its earnings outlook and stronger device demand. Investors have also responded positively to expectations of improving cost conditions and the company's upbeat revenue forecast. The stock gave up some ground in early premarket trading on Thursday, slipping 0.15% at the time of writing. Microsoft (MSFT): Microsoft's latest earnings and continued growth in its Azure cloud business helped drive the stock to a 52-week high on Wednesday. Adding to the optimism, Bill Ackman's Pershing Square said in its third-quarter investor letter that Microsoft is well-positioned to benefit from growing AI adoption through Azure, Copilot, and GitHub. The stock was up 0.08% in early premarket trading on Thursday. AppLovin (APP): The stock was among the biggest premarket gainers on Thursday after the advertising technology company reported record third-quarter results on Wednesday. Revenue jumped 55% year over year, while net income rose 72%. The stock had already gained 10% during Wednesday's regular session and climbed around 18% in Thursday’s premarket trading. Nvidia (NVDA): Nvidia faced renewed pressure as concerns over tighter AI regulations and possible delays in data center projects weighed on semiconductor stocks. The prospect of stricter rules under the incoming political landscape has raised questions about the pace of AI infrastructure spending. Investors are also debating the sustainability of the sector's rapid expansion, including concerns over circular financing and off-balance-sheet debt used to fund large AI hardware purchases. Nvidia shares were down around 1% in early premarket trading on Thursday. IREN (IREN): The stock remained on traders' radar after coming under heavy selling pressure on Wednesday, with shares plunging 11.4% during the regular session. The decline came as cloud and AI stocks faced pressure following Democrats' midterm victory. The company also faced scrutiny after a report linked its business to Microsoft's lower AI capital spending in the previous quarter. IREN shares fell around 1.3% in early premarket trading on Thursday. Fastly (FSLY), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Credo Technology (CRDO) were among the other trending tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing on Thursday. Investors will be tracking a fresh batch of corporate earnings, with DraftKings (DKNG), Novavax (NVAX), GoPro (GPRO), Tapestry (TPR), Airbnb (ABNB) and Akamai (AKAM) among the companies scheduled to report on Thursday. Meanwhile, weekly jobless claims will be in focus on Thursday, ahead of the October nonfarm payrolls report due on Friday. Retail sentiment showed mixed trends across major index ETFs over the past 24 hours. Sentiment toward SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500, improved to ‘bearish’ from ‘extremely bearish,’ while for Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, it remained ‘bearish’. Meanwhile, sentiment toward the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) turned ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’. Arthur Hayes expects "insiders unlock and dump" to flood SpaceX (SPCX) stock, then follow suit with Anthropic (ANT) and OpenAI (OPEAZZX), triggering a credit squeeze that ends in a central bank bailout that lifts crypto and makes Bitcoin (BTC) ‘glorious’ in the long run. Hayes made the case Thursday in a Substack essay called "D For Dilution." In his essay, he said the three companies' stocks would struggle as locked-up shares held by insiders become free to trade. Then falling share prices will make it harder for the companies to borrow, tightening the dollar liquidity crypto depends on, Hayes wrote. "This presents an issue for the general market environment because the entire AI trade rests on vibes. The vibes surrounding whether you believe the lofty future profitability and ubiquity of AI determine whether you lend money to the industry," Hayes added. Hayes compared the setup to Zcash (ZEC) back in 2016. Early adopters bought at high prices with a small amount of the token available, and most are still underwater even as Zcash's market value has grown since. You don't trade the market cap; you trade the price per token," he wrote. ZEC’s price was up over 2%, trading around $1,318. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ZEC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day. SpaceX's stock price has been relatively stable since its initial public offering, but the number of publicly traded shares has increased by about 50%, Hayes said. He projected that some 8.6 billion additional shares will be available by the end of June 2027. That would increase the float by roughly another 50%, mostly because of the vesting of the shares held by Elon Musk. The rumored combination of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA) could mean about a 50% dilution for Class A shareholders, Hayes said. The stock can only be supported with an increase in free cash flow, Hayes said. He also said Musk would have to return that cash through dividends or buybacks. Anthropic filed its S-1, the registration statement a company submits to U.S. regulators before an IPO, in late October and intends to go public on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. An AI agent looked at the filing on his behalf, Hayes said. There's no near-term dividend expectation, he said, and the company will plow its money into about $900 billion of compute commitments. Based on that schedule, Hayes wrote, "it is almost impossible mathematically for the stock price to go up between listing and June 2027." He figured that the selloff would take about $1.245 trillion in new money to absorb the price if Anthropic is valued at $1.5 trillion at market. Hayes also said investors should think of Anthropic as an oil and gas company rather than a software company, given customers pay for usage and past spending doesn't guarantee future demand. This comes as investors were already pushing ANT's IPO valuation from $ 1.6 trillion to $2 trillion. Hayes said OpenAI "will be the worst of the bunch." Hayes said that OpenAI has a more concentrated customer base and a higher burn rate than Anthropic. He noted reports that the company had cut its fundraising target from $30 billion to $20 billion and its valuation from $1.5 trillion to $1.25 trillion. Hayes believes a future OpenAI IPO would be structured similarly to SpaceX and Anthropic, with a small float and heavy insider sales in the months ahead. Companies can't borrow money in the debt markets on their own. They have to be publicly traded, Hayes said. If their shares fall, lenders will demand higher yields. That would eat into those loans, Hayes said, who said bank loans powered the crypto rally that began in August. Last week, the U.S. bank balance sheets contracted, we observed. "This is the transmission channel from AI to crypto." His family office, Maelstrom, will stay clear, said Hayes. He believes the central banks will print money once the AI slump turns into a crisis threat. That, he said, "will be glorious for Bitcoin and crypto holders. But be patient." Bitcoin’s price was up over 3%, trading around $80,300 over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ over the past day. Wall Street analysts turned bullish on Navitas Semiconductor (NVTS), Duolingo (DUOL) and Fiserv (FISV), citing AI infrastructure demand, user growth and improving business performance. Meanwhile, CleanSpark (CLSK) faced fresh concerns over Texas' political shift and potential regulatory delays, while deal-related uncertainty prompted rating cuts for Lumentum (LITE) and Roku (ROKU). Craig-Hallum upgraded Navitas Semiconductor stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ and kept its $13 price target. The firm cited new customer wins, a growing order backlog and strong AI infrastructure spending. It also sees the Claros acquisition as another potential growth driver. Rosenblatt also upgraded Navitas to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ but kept its $13 price target. The firm said the company beat Q3 estimates by a wide margin as its high-power business picked up speed. Orders exceeded shipments, and its backlog now extends through mid-2027. Rosenblatt believes Claros' integrated voltage regulator technology could help Navitas address power-management needs for next-generation AI processors. Navitas’ Q3 revenue jumped 38% year-on-year to $14 million and loss narrowed to $0.03 per share. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’. Wells Fargo analyst Alec Brondolo raised Duolingo stock to ‘Equal Weight’ from ‘Underweight’ and increased the price target to $120 from $80. The firm highlighted 29% annual growth in daily active users during the third quarter, suggesting the company may have exited September with growth above 30%. Wells Fargo also believes Duolingo has successfully offset weaker viral marketing momentum through product launches, brand collaborations and live initiatives. The firm now sees potential for bookings growth in the mid-teens by 2027. Truist raised its price target to $170 from $120 but kept a ‘Hold’ rating. The firm expects user growth to stay strong next quarter, giving Duolingo more chances to earn revenue from its growing user base. Retail sentiment toward the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Argus analyst Jasper Hellweg upgraded Fiserv stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Hold’ and set a $72 price target. The firm pointed to better Q3 results, especially fewer customers leaving its banking business. Fiserv is also adding more customer-facing employees and stepping up spending on AI and technology upgrades to improve its platforms. TD Cowen raised its price target to $59 from $49 but kept a ‘Hold’ rating, saying better execution suggests Fiserv's business is recovering. RBC Capital also increased its target to $70 from $65 while maintaining its ‘Outperform’ rating. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Lumentum stock faced analyst downgrades after agreeing to an all-stock $115 billion combination with Marvell Technology (MRVL). Stifel lowered Lumentum to ‘Hold’ from ‘Buy’ and cut its price target to $806 from $1,232. The firm expects the stock to track Marvell's performance and the transaction's valuation spread, leaving limited room for independent gains. The deal is expected to close during the first half of 2028. B. Riley also moved LITE to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Buy’, setting a $770 target. Bernstein reduced its price target to $900 from $1,220 but maintained ‘Outperform’. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Rosenblatt downgraded Roku stock to ‘Neutral’ from ‘Buy’ and set a $160 price target as the firm expects the deal with Fox Corp. (FOXA) to close sooner than the previously expected mid-2027 timeline, after Fox signaled it wants to complete the transaction as quickly as possible. Roku shares are trading near the $160 value agreed in the deal, leaving limited room for further gains as investors wait for the merger to close. Retail investors remained ‘bullish’ on the stock. CleanSpark stock was downgraded after Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race. Keefe Bruyette lowered its rating on CleanSpark to ‘Market Perform’ from ‘Outperform’ and cut its price target to $9.50 from $11.50. The firm warned that regulatory uncertainty could delay data center leases and project agreements. Bernstein analyst Gautam Chhugani cut CleanSpark's price target to $11 from $24 but maintained ‘Outperform’. The analyst noted that more than half of the power portfolios held by several cryptocurrency miners expanding into AI infrastructure are concentrated in Texas. According to Bernstein, Hinojosa's victory could prolong the restrictions and create legislative uncertainty, potentially slowing project development across the sector. AMC Entertainment Holdings (AMC) stock is heading for its best weekly gain since July, after the theater chain posted record third-quarter (Q3) revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and CEO Adam Aron declared on X that AMC “has recovered”—a stock attempting to claw back four years of losses. AMC Entertainment stock traded over 2% lower overnight, ahead of Thursday. The stock has gained 15% so far this week and is on track to reverse four years of losses. The rally tests whether a record quarter can change how Wall Street prices a company that spent years as a survival story. AMC still reported a nine-month GAAP net loss, and its stock trades at a valuation unlike its peers’. Aron is betting that a $10 billion-plus box office makes the old debt and dilution worries obsolete. For the better part of four years, AMC Entertainment’s story was about staying alive. This week, its CEO argued that story is over. “Today, we can finally say that AMC has recovered,” Aron posted on X after the company reported Q3 results on Wednesday. He called the quarter “a triumph” and said AMC’s biggest and best in its 106-year history. The numbers back him on growth. Q3 revenue rose 31.6% year-on-year to $1.711 billion, up from $1.300 billion last year. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 183.7% to $347.5 million, nearly triple last year’s figure. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 20.3%, more than double the 9.4% from a year ago. It was the second straight quarter in which AMC set all-time company records for both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. Analysts had expected about $1.62 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.10 a share, according to Fiscal.ai estimates cited by Stocktwits. AMC reported adjusted earnings of $0.13, against a loss of 58 cents a year ago. Operating cash flow was $176.6 million, versus a $14.9 million outflow a year ago. Free cash flow was $109.3 million, which brings the year-to-date total to $124.7 million. That is why Aron sees AMC posting positive free cash flow for all of 2026. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to $751.9 million, excluding $39.6 million in restricted cash. Attendance did the heavy lifting. Q3 attendance rose 28.3% to 74.9 million moviegoers, with international markets up 41.5% and U.S. markets up 23.3%. AMC did this with slightly fewer screens, averaging 9,177 versus 9,354 a year ago. The company also reported record revenue per patron, which Aron credited to its loyalty programs and its growing roster of premium large-format auditoriums. Aron also leaned on the balance sheet. On Oct. 5, AMC completed a $3.97 billion refinancing covering about 97% of its debt, pushing maturities out to late 2031 and 2033. During the Q3 earnings call, Aron addressed critics directly. He called any future article describing AMC as overly debt-laden “mindlessly in error.” He said “groundless fears of endless share dilution will come only from those looking in the rearview mirror.” He did not rule out new stock sales, saying AMC will “wisely utilize equity financings when it makes sense.” His argument rests on the macro backdrop. AMC now operates in a box office above $10 billion, he said, “a very different animal” from the $7 billion to $9 billion range of the past four years. Q4 looks strong so far. Aron said October’s domestic box office ran about 35% above the same month last year. The remaining slate includes The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Dune: Part Three, Avengers: Doomsday and Jumanji: Open World. He expects the domestic and global box office to reach their highest full-year levels in seven years. AMC has gained about 125% in 2026 as of late October, ahead of IMAX (IMAX), Cinemark (CNK) and streaming giant Netflix (NFLX). Even with record quarters, its first nine months produced a net loss of $19.2 million, or $0.03 share. Nine-month adjusted net earnings were a modest $26.9 million. Until GAAP profits become consistent, valuation arguments for AMC will rest on EBITDA and cash flow rather than earnings. The next few months will decide whether this week’s 15% gain is the start of a re-rating. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory the previous day. The stock has registered a 192% increase in message volume over the past week. Another user said, “$109.3 million in quarterly free cash flow with expectation for positive free cash flow for all of 2026! Stay Zen AMC family. Our time will come.” AMC stock has gained 40% in the past twelve months. Read Next: Why Did AAPL, MSFT, AMC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs? SpaceX’s (SPCX) wireless expansion and AI financing, Rocket Lab’s (RKLB) 99th Electron launch and AST SpaceMobile’s (ASTS) Chilean approval have driven space-sector news so far this week, alongside mixed earnings from Redwire (RDW) and Voyager Technologies (VOYG). SpaceX’s mobile ambitions moved forward with Qualcomm’s selection to power Starlink Mobile’s nationwide terrestrial 5G network. Deployment begins in 2027, with tens of thousands of sites planned. “This is a significant win for our infrastructure business and the beginning of a strategic relationship with tremendous potential,” Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said. The chipmaker expects revenue to begin near the end of fiscal 2027 and develop more fully in fiscal 2028. SpaceX also reportedly explored buying EchoStar’s Boost Mobile or accessing its network, though transferring leased network access could require carrier consent. Alongside its wireless expansion, SpaceX is financing a larger AI buildout. Goldman Sachs and Apollo are seeking buyers for portions of its $40 billion chip financing, covering leased Nvidia Vera Rubin equipment expected in the first half of 2027. SemiAnalysis said SpaceX’s 13GW computing-capacity target for 2027 looked achievable, identifying more than 9GW across sites and 3.6GW under construction, while flagging power constraints. Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire, whose firm backs SpaceX, projected $731.1 billion in 2028 revenue in his investor model. “I think we can do better,” CEO Elon Musk replied. Morgan Stanley separately brought forward its projected free-cash-flow breakeven to 2031 from 2035. However, Musk’s growth ambitions face political and deal risks. Sen.Ted Cruz warned of subpoenas targeting Musk, while Gary Black cautioned that falling shares in an all-stock acquirer could erode the target shareholders’ takeover premium. Retail sentiment for SPCX improved to ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ last week, amid ‘high’ message volume. Shares are down 16% so far this year. Rocket Lab moved within one flight of Electron’s 100th launch on Monday, deploying iQPS’s WADATSUMI-II radar-imaging satellite. “The Sea God Surveys” marked its 20th mission of 2026 and tenth successful iQPS launch, with eight more dedicated missions booked through 2030. The launch momentum supported Citizens’ bullish stance. The firm reiterated ‘Market Outperform’ and a $90 target, viewing Neutron’s delay as a timing setback and expecting its debut in late fiscal second-quarter 2027. However, its broader expansion is still under scrutiny. Globalstar raised potential supplier conflicts surrounding the Iridium takeover, while Rocket Lab and Iridium argued that separate SpaceX and Ligado concerns predate the merger. Space Systems head Brad Clevenger also discussed commercial space and national security with Sen.Kevin Cramer at Wednesday’s UND summit. Separately, disclosures showed CFO Adam Spice sold 140,157 shares for $7.4 million after exercising options, while director Nina Armagno sold 10,926 shares. Both Monday sales followed previously adopted trading plans. Retail sentiment turned ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’ last week, amid ‘normal’ message volume. Shares are down 25% so far this year. AST and AT&T announced Monday “the industry’s first” successful terrestrial-to-satellite cellular handoff. The test from last month in Washington maintained a connection between the networks, supported by Ericsson and Nokia. “The successful handoff is a significant milestone, but it’s not the finish line,” AT&T network executive Robert Walters said, as the companies progress toward beta services. AST also expanded its regulatory footprint with a 30-year nationwide Chilean concession. Its 24-month first-stage service timetable, measured from Tuesday’s publication, points to November 2028. As AST advances, competition is adding urgency. “AST SpaceMobile needs to pivot, and pivot FAST,” Boost Mobile founder Peter Adderton said, urging partnerships with experienced mobile-brand operators. Ownership disclosures entering the week showed Vanguard held 15.33 million shares, or 5.11%, as of September 30, while Rakuten Investment Management increased its quarter-end holding 23.9% to 17,156 shares. Retail sentiment remained ‘bearish’ compared with last week, amid ‘low’ message volume. Shares are down 51% so far this year. Redwire’s third-quarter (Q3) revenue rose 5.4% to $109 million, falling short of the $126.56 million consensus estimate, while its loss of $0.09 per share matched expectations. The results also showed a record $619.7 million backlog and record gross margin of 32.3%, up from 16.3% a year earlier. Contract awards totaled $188.7 million, producing a 1.73 book-to-bill ratio. “Although revenue timing continues to be uneven, with another quarter of record gross margins expanding from 16.3% to 32.3% year-over-year, the quality of our revenue is improving as we deliver mission-critical products and solutions across multiple domains,” CEO Peter Cannito said. Redwire maintained its fiscal 2026 revenue outlook of $450 million to $500 million, versus consensus of $475.28 million. It posted a $23.2 million net loss and a $5.3 million adjusted EBITDA loss. Retail sentiment jumped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ last week, amid ‘high’ message volume. Shares are up 2% so far this year. Voyager’s third-quarter revenue jumped 124% to $89 million, beating the $81.38 million consensus estimate. Its adjusted loss of $0.87 per share was slightly wider than the expected $0.86 loss. The company raised its fiscal 2026 revenue outlook to $287 million to $305 million from $275 million to 305 million, against consensus of $291.51 million. Supporting that outlook, backlog reached a record $742 million, including $347 million from Astrobotic, while bookings hit a record $116 million. “Our record backlog provides meaningful multi-year revenue visibility and raising our full-year guidance reflects this momentum,” CEO Dylan Taylor said. Starlab’s signed commercial reservations totaled $700 million, though Voyager posted a $55.7 million net loss attributable to the company. Beyond earnings, Voyager won a five-year, $35 million NASA HUNCH management contract Wednesday and appointed retired Space Force Gen.B. Chance Saltzman as board-of-advisors chairman Monday. title: Why The Blue Tsunami Rattled AI Stocks - Investor's Business Daily

BREAKING: Stock Market Suffers Damaging Weekly Losses The trillion-dollar AI data center boom will likely face even greater scrutiny after Democrats won control over Congress and governors' mansions in several key states. The results have shaken AI stocks, highlighted by the past week's volatile trading. The Nasdaq tumbled sharply Thursday, before bouncing back Friday. Top AI stocks are set to close the week lower while the cloud giants also had a wild ride, with volatile trading for Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT) and Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL).  The action underscores the challenges ahead for the AI megatrend after a Blue Tsunami election. Backlash to data centers — which act as the engines powering AI technology — has led to calls for moratoriums, bans and other legislation. The results in Texas were particularly striking. Ed Mills, the Washington D.C. policy analyst for Raymond James, said what happened in the Lone Star state, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, could prove most impactful for AI stocks. Risk Management: How Invested In The Market Should You Be Right Now? "To use a different storm analogy, this is arguably a category five hurricane that hit the data center trade," Mills told Investor's Business Daily. "You have a candidate that has won, who said that the old moratorium was a scam and that, if elected, she would put in place a real moratorium. Now that's just Texas, but you also have a similar thing in Ohio." Hinojosa made opposition to data centers a key part of her winning campaign for Texas governor. She called for a broader moratorium on data centers until new legislation is passed. She was critical of a freeze Abbott placed on permits earlier this year. Additionally, she argues he would lift it following the election. Texas trails only Virginia for total data centers active or in the works, according to estimates from Pew Research. It is also the site of massive data center efforts such as the Abilene Stargate campus. Amy Acton in Ohio and Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia also made data centers a campaign issue. Following the midterms, research firm Cleanview found 41% of the current U.S. data center pipeline is located in states that have a governor or governor-elect pledging restrictions on the facilities. Data center backlash will bring challenges to Amazon, Microsoft and Google. The tech giants are the three leading cloud-computing providers. Each so-called cloud hyperscaler is spending hundreds of billions to build new data centers to meet demand. But the stock reactions following the midterms point to a more nuanced picture. Amazon, Microsoft and Google actually rallied on Wednesday. Then they pulled back sharply with the rest of the AI trade Thursday. On the one hand, restrictions on new data centers likely provide an edge to the biggest, most established cloud computing providers. Hyperscalers are the AI incumbents, as Needham analyst Laura Martin wrote to clients following the midterms. "We believe higher regulatory barriers entrench incumbents, and increase risks (and raise required ROICs) for new entrants," Martin wrote, referring to return on invested capital. Investors may not be all that upset if AI spending is forced to slow. Soaring capital costs have eaten the free-cash-flow of even tech's biggest players, raising concern on Wall Street in the lead-up to the elections. Some tech investors will view the midterms as a "slight positive" if the results force Big Tech to "hit the slow down button" on capital spending, Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives wrote on Wednesday. At the same time, AI demand has helped accelerate revenue growth for each of the three leading cloud businesses. Restrictions on data centers risk either raising costs or making it more difficult to meet demand. Meta Platforms (META) President Dina Powell McCormick said at a Wall Street Journal conference on Wednesday that building data centers in the U.S. is "going to be harder" following the midterm results. Tech companies may look to international markets, she added. While it doesn't operate an enterprise cloud infrastructure business, Meta is spending hundreds of billions on data centers to support its AI ambitions and massive portfolio of social media apps. The midterms fallout was also pronounced for companies that provide components used for the AI buildout, from chips and computer hardware to energy and construction. Nvidia (NVDA) stock fell sharply Thursday, its worst day since it tumbled after the release of Chinese AI model DeepSeek in January 2025. Nvidia also bounced back Friday, but was on track for a weekly loss. Other leading AI players also had a volatile week. Shares of Seagate (STX), Dell (DELL), Micron (MU) and CoreWeave (CRWV) were also poised to end the week in the red. Analysts with UBS estimate that data center pauses or moratoriums could put about 30% of the capacity previous expected in 2028 at risk. "The slowdown is a negative for Semis and AI infrastructure, but a lot is already priced into semis with valuations nearing multiyear lows," UBS strategist Keith Parker wrote in a client research note Wednesday. SpaceX (SPCX) is also a major developer of cloud infrastructure and AI.  Shares fell 4% Wednesday and 9% Thursday before regaining some ground Friday. Investors are also likely bracing for blowback from Elon Musk's big donations to Republican politicians. Investors are likely still sizing up the broader impact for AI stocks. Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani said in a client note that increased scarcity could drive up prices for AI compute. Amazon, Google and Microsoft are poised to close the week higher. Amazon offered a bullish signal Wednesday by breaking a recent downward trendline drawn from a record high reached on Aug. 3. That was followed by a pullback Thursday and slight gain Friday. Microsoft jumped up from a test of its 50-day moving average Wednesday before easing back by 3.5% Thursday. Microsoft is the top-rated among the hyperscaler stocks with a best-possible 99 IBD Composite Rating, according to IBD Stock Checkup. The score combines five separate proprietary ratings into one rating. The best growth stocks have a Composite Rating of 90 or better. Google stock is still trading near recent lows that followed its Q3 earnings, despite the gains Wednesday. Nvidia is sharply below its 200-day moving average with the postelection tumble. Meanwhile, Raymond James' Mills said the backlash to data centers is tied to factors that extend well beyond the structures themselves. They have also come to represent concerns about AI's impact on jobs and even national security. "In a lot of these conversations, you see as much as 75% of the American people opposed to data centers," Mills said. "And it's not just because of affordability. It's not just because of environmental issues. It is the physical manifestation related to a lot of anxieties all wrapped up into one." That could make both data centers and AI fertile ground for politicians to run against in future elections. title: The AI infrastructure boom faces a "global crackdown": restrictions on construction are crossing the Atlantic, with Microsoft's (MSFT.US) Amsterdam project at the eye of the storm. - 富途牛牛
content: The wave of restrictions on AI data center construction, triggered by the U.S. midterm elections, is spreading across the Atlantic to Europe. The wave of restrictions on AI data center construction triggered by the U.S. midterm elections is spreading across the Atlantic to Europe. Zhitong Finance APP has learned that on Friday local time, a group of protesters broke into a Microsoft (MSFT.US) data center construction site in Amsterdam, kicking off a two-day rally. This is part of a growing global backlash against the rapid expansion of computing power required for AI. According to the "Stop Dirty Data Centres" coalition, activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday. The coalition brings together environmental organizations and digital rights movements to jointly call for a moratorium on large-scale construction. Reportedly, over 100 activists gathered at a Microsoft AI data center construction site in Amsterdam on Friday. They marched arm-in-arm, then breached the site, climbed construction cranes, hung balloons, and danced inside while police monitored from the sidelines. Some demonstrators held signs reading: "Tear down your data centers." The site owner, Pure Data Centres, plans to invest over $1 billion, with backing from Oaktree Capital, a subsidiary of Brookfield. The company stated it is committed to engaging with local stakeholders. "We urge those on-site to evacuate safely and engage in dialogue with us regarding this project and the concerns raised," the company said. Other planned protests include marches in Dublin, demonstrations outside the parliament building in Warsaw, and another protest targeting a Microsoft data center in Denmark. Microsoft stated that it understands the strong public opinions surrounding the project and respects the right to peaceful expression, but does not support any illegal activities. Tech stocks face sell-off amid market concerns over tightening AI regulation From Spain to India and the United States, resistance is gaining momentum. Driven by market fears that Democratic control of Congress could lead to stricter regulations stifling the AI boom, U.S. tech stocks fell sharply on Thursday. Senator Bernie Sanders' earlier proposal for a "national moratorium on new data centers," combined with the explicit commitment by the governor-elect of Texas—one of the most important hubs for AI data centers in the U.S.—to pause approvals for new projects, jointly triggered this "reckoning-style" sell-off across the AI supply chain. Protesters argue that data centers exacerbate strains on electricity and water resources, compete with housing and other industries for scarce resources, and hinder the achievement of climate goals. They also highlight risks of job losses, the concentration of computing power in the hands of large tech companies, and potential threats to personal and national security. Tech companies responded that data centers are the core infrastructure for meeting global demand for AI and cloud computing, serving as critical facilities for enterprises, governments, and general consumers. The “Stop Dirty Data Centres” coalition emphasized that it does not oppose technological progress nor call for the shutdown of existing data centers; rather, it advocates pausing new large-scale projects until clear regulatory frameworks are established in respective countries. In response, Europe faces internal contradictions: on one hand, it seeks to catch up with AI development in the United States and Asia to boost productivity; on the other, it aims to maintain relatively strict regulatory and public protection mechanisms. Henna Virkkunen, the EU’s top digital official, stated in an interview on Thursday that Europe needs more data centers to support AI development, but construction must proceed prudently. “AI is undoubtedly a crucial technology, and we must possess sovereign computing capabilities.” Virkkunen noted that Europe is ramping up chip manufacturing and investment in AI startups, with plans to establish a number of large-scale computing facilities within the region. However, she added, “For the public, one point is crucial: people must be assured that electricity bills will not skyrocket due to data centers, that power outages will not be triggered by computing infrastructure, and that such projects must not harm the environment.” It is reported that Google’s (GOOGL.US) project in Finland has been subject to a criminal investigation over land-clearing issues; Italy and Portugal are tightening environmental regulations for data centers; and Microsoft previously withdrew from a data center project in the UK due to delays in infrastructure development. title: What Are Microsoft Investors Betting On? - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Microsoft (MSFT) stock trades at 26.8 times its adjusted earnings over the last twelve months. This profit figure leaves out one-time items and adds back stock-based pay after tax. That is a lot to pay for a single year of profit, and the multiple is about the same, 26.7 times, against the profit analysts expect for fiscal 2027. That forecast may not add back stock-based pay, so it may count profit on a different basis. The stock only looks cheaper against fiscal 2028 profit. So what kind of growth are you paying for at today’s price? The consensus forecast projects Microsoft’s revenue rising about 19% in fiscal 2027, to $395 billion. For fiscal 2028, the forecast anticipates sales growth of 20.5% and net income growth of 20.9%. The forecast’s net margin is 37.7% in fiscal 2027 and 37.8% in fiscal 2028. This means the profit growth you are betting on comes from more sales, not from wider margins. Based on the consensus forecast, Microsoft stock trades at 26.7 times fiscal 2027 earnings and 22.1 times fiscal 2028 earnings. Its trailing multiple on adjusted earnings is 26.8 times. Has Microsoft Delivered Sales Growth Near The Forecast? For fiscal 2027, Microsoft is close. Revenue grew 18.8% in fiscal Q1 2027, and management guided for growth of 18% to 19% in fiscal Q2. Over the last twelve months, though, revenue grew 17.9%. This means the fiscal 2028 forecast expects faster sales growth than Microsoft has delivered. That growth is uneven across the business. In fiscal 2026, Microsoft’s Intelligent Cloud segment grew 29.7%, while its More Personal Computing segment shrank 1.1%. Microsoft reported a net margin of 40.3% in fiscal 2026. The consensus forecast has a lower margin in both coming years. The forecast does not specify whether its profit is reported or adjusted, meaning the two margins may not be measured the same way. The likeliest place is data center capacity. On its October 28 call, management said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, and some third-party GPU capacity Microsoft was counting on for fiscal Q2 has moved into the second half of the fiscal year. Management guided for Azure growth of 49% to 50% in fiscal Q2 and said Microsoft needs further efficiency gains across its fleet to reach it. Any further delay would leave Microsoft less to sell and pull the sales forecast down. Microsoft has worked around these delays once already: Azure revenue grew 48% in fiscal Q1 2027, ahead of management’s expectations, even with third-party capacity arriving late. Price is the other place the forecast could slip. Management said the price Microsoft gets per token, a unit of AI work, can change through the quarter. Foundry, its platform for building AI agents, more than tripled its revenue from a year earlier in fiscal Q1 2027. Management named higher revenue per token as one reason Foundry beat expectations. A fall in that price would pull the sales forecast down too. If Microsoft delivers the consensus forecast, the multiples on fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 earnings are a fair picture of what you pay for the stock. If capacity arrives late or token prices slip, profit could fall short of the forecast. Those multiples would then understate what you pay, making the stock a riskier bet. Azure growth against management’s guide is the number to watch, and Microsoft is expected to report it in January 2027. Forecasts can slip, and so can markets. Build a portfolio that holds up either way. After a run like this, the hard questions are personal: hold, trim or sell, and the tax on each. title: Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) Compounds Nscale's IPO Troubles By Walking Away From Texas Data Center Expansion - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By Ewan Scott | Nov 5, 2026 | Economy & Business, Energy, Featured, News & Analysis Nscale’s path to a public listing is narrowing as Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) declines to exercise an option that would have more than doubled their existing computing agreement at a Texas data center. Reuters reported Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter, that the decision was made several months ago, predating Nscale’s IPO filing in September. Microsoft’s existing workflow under the original contract remains intact, and the Texas pullback does not alter the terms of the deal already in force. The two companies signed an agreement in 2025 for Nscale to deploy roughly 200,000 Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) AI chips across its data centers in both Europe and the United States. The Texas decision is the second significant retreat by Microsoft from Nscale commitments, following its exit last month from a deal to anchor Nscale’s flagship Essex, UK data center project. Power connection delays at the Essex site pushed the expected supply date into the 2030s, prompting Microsoft to walk away from that anchor arrangement entirely. Nscale, which counts Nvidia among its backers, is already under pressure from investors who have pushed back on its $130 billion IPO valuation target, according to a report published last month. The broader cloud sector is adding to the anxiety, with debt-laden neocloud operators such as CoreWeave drawing increased scrutiny amid persistent concerns about overcapacity across the industry. Political headwinds are also emerging, as the Democrats’ decisive midterm victory introduces the prospect of stricter AI regulation that could make new data center construction harder and more expensive. Separately, delays tied to IREN Ltd (NASDAQ: IREN) were cited by The Information as a factor in Microsoft spending less than it had budgeted for capital expenditures in its most recent quarter. Retail traders on Stocktwits have turned negative on the stock, with sentiment flipping to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish,’ and one trader captured the market’s mood bluntly: “$MSFT microsoft jumped 6% today on a bet the build slows down. seems like the best ai news left is less ai spending, and a rally for not building tells you where the capex story actually stands.” Despite the turbulence, MSFT shares remain up 15.6% year to date through their last closing price, reflecting how broader market enthusiasm for AI has so far outweighed concerns about infrastructure execution. title: Microsoft Stock Has Gained More Than 50% in About 4 Months. Here's What It Has Usually Done Next. - The Motley Fool
content: The software giant has run this fast 13 times before. How did the following year usually go? Microsoft (MSFT -0.99%) shares jumped nearly 7% on Wednesday, Nov. 4, as U.S. stocks rallied the day after Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections. The stock sits near $553 as of this writing. That leaves it about 57% over its June 25 close of $352.83, and the rise took just 92 trading days. A move like that is rare for a company worth about $4 trillion. But Microsoft has done it before. Going back through its daily closing prices to 1986, I find 13 past runs like this one. In 11 of them, the stock was up a year later, with a median one-year gain of around 33%. It's a solid record. But it might mean less than it seems. Microsoft stock has climbed in around 74% of all one-year periods since 1986, fast run or not. And the latest run, in July 2025, is one of the two that finished down. Every run starts the first day Microsoft closed at least 50% over its lowest close in the past 92 trading days. I used split-adjusted prices without dividends, and runs had to begin at least one year apart. "A year later" is the close 12 months after a run started (or the last trading day before it). By this rule, the current run began on Oct. 6. Ten of the 13 past runs came between 1986 and 2001, when Microsoft was a much smaller company. The biggest years came in that stretch, too. Shares more than doubled over the year after the runs that began in November 1986, January 1991, and March 1998. Somebody is going to make a fortune on Anthropic’s IPO. It probably won’t be regular investors waiting for the day it goes public. Unless investors know where to look. Because two companies anyone can buy today already own pieces of Anthropic. And one of them owns a piece of OpenAI, too. The one early miss followed a January 1988 run, when the stock was recovering from the October 1987 crash, and shares were around 12% down a year later. Since the 2001 run, Microsoft has only moved this fast three times. The stock gained around 12% over the year after June 2009 and about 33% after June 2020. Then it lost about 13% after July 2025. Even some of the good years were rough. After the January 1992 and January 2001 runs, shares slid over 20% at one point before ending the year higher. Microsoft's latest fast run hit the 50% mark the day after its fiscal 2025 fourth-quarter report on July 30, 2025. The July 31 close of $533.50 was around 50% over the April 8 low. Investors paid about 38 times earnings then, using the $14.13 a share Microsoft earned in fiscal 2025 on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis. Shares drifted mostly sideways over a few months. Then they fell all the way to that $352.83 close on June 25, 2026 -- around 34% below where the run began. Even a 15% gain the day after Microsoft's fiscal 2026 report in late July didn't erase the loss, and on July 31, 2026, shares were still about 13% down from a year earlier. I'd say the starting price mattered more than the pace of the run. At around 38 times earnings, the shares could fall a long way on any hint of trouble. In a couple of ways, I think it is. Adjusted earnings per share grew 22% in fiscal 2026, and the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended Sept. 30, 2026) added another 18% gain, to $4.89. For the past four reported quarters, adjusted earnings were about $18.04 a share. At roughly $553, the stock costs about 31 times adjusted earnings, well under the 38 times earnings investors paid in July 2025. Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing platform, is also accelerating. Its revenue climbed 40% year over year in the quarter that ended September 2025, then 42% in the quarter that ended this June and 48% in the last one. Of course, that growth takes a lot of money. Microsoft's cash from operations rose 29% from a year ago. But free cash flow dropped about 27% to $18.6 billion as the company poured more cash into data centers. What has Microsoft stock usually done after a run like this? It has usually kept rising. But that record only modestly beats the stock's odds in any given year, and the most recent case went the other way. The business looks stronger than it did in July 2025, and the stock is cheaper relative to its earnings. Still, with free cash flow shrinking, paying about 31 times adjusted earnings just after a 57% run isn't something I'm eager to do. title: Election Results And Falling Oil Prices Fuel Broad Market Rally As Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) And Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) Flash Buy Signals - Foreign Policy Journal
content: By David Prior | Nov 5, 2026 | Economy & Business, Energy, Featured, News & Analysis, Politics A twin catalyst of election outcomes and sharply lower crude oil prices drove a powerful postelection stock market surge on Wednesday, lifting equities across a wide range of sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average led the charge with a gain of 3.03%, signaling strong investor confidence in the post-election economic outlook as capital rotated aggressively into blue-chip names. Oil futures told a parallel story, with the benchmark crude contract declining 0.94%, easing cost pressures for businesses and consumers alike and adding further fuel to the broader rally. While the headline indexes surged, the picture inside the technology sector was more complicated, with many tech stocks retreating even as select mega-cap names broke sharply higher. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) posted a gain of 5.15%, with the stock flashing a clear buy signal that caught the attention of traders looking to position ahead of further postelection momentum. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) outpaced even Apple’s move, climbing 5.66% and triggering its own buy signal, reinforcing the view that institutional money was selectively rotating into the largest and most liquid technology names. Amazon also joined the group of stocks generating buy signals during the session, adding a third mega-cap name to what analysts described as a meaningful cluster of technical breakouts. Meta Platforms offered a more muted performance, gaining just 0.38%, underscoring the uneven nature of the rally even within the top tier of the technology universe. Stocks across many non-technology sectors were among the session’s clearest winners, with buy signals emerging broadly as investors responded to the combination of political clarity and lower energy costs. Market watchers cautioned, however, that at least one sector was best avoided despite the overall bullish tone, suggesting that not every corner of the market was positioned to benefit equally from the postelection environment. The divergence between the surging Dow and the mixed performance within tech highlights a broader rotation that investors will need to navigate carefully as the post-election landscape takes shape in the days ahead. David Prior is a senior reporter at the Foreign Policy Journal, covering everything from current affairs and global politics to stock market news and analysis.

title: After Pulling Deal For Nscale’s UK Data Center, Microsoft Rejects Texas Expansion Option: Report - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) will not exercise an option to more than double ​its existing agreement with AI cloud provider Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center, Reuters reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter. The companies struck a deal last year for Nscale to deploy around 200,000 Nvidia (NVDA) AI chips with Microsoft ​across its data centers in Europe and the U.S. The reported development signals more pain for the IPO-bound Nscale. Last month, Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's flagship data center project in ‌Essex, the UK, after ⁠power connection delays pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s. Nscale, backed by Nvidia, filed for an IPO in September, although a report last month said it faced opposition from investors over its $130 billion IPO valuation target. Reuters reported that Microsoft's decision to not expand the Texas contract was made ​several months ago, before Nscale filed for its IPO, and that its existing workflow, as per the original, was not affected. The development comes as the cloud industry faces increased scrutiny. In recent weeks, the debt-heavy model of neocloud firms such as CoreWeave has come under the scanner even as concerns prevail over overcapacity. The decisive midterm win by the Democrats, who are seen to be pro-AI regulation, has added concerns that new data centers will be harder and costlier to build. That could stifle the growth in cloud capacity essential to support AI. Meanwhile, the delays in bringing new cloud capacity online are also drawing attention. The Information reported on Wednesday that delays from IREN Ltd (IREN) contributed to Microsoft spending less than it had earmarked in capital expenditures last quarter. AMC Entertainment Holdings (AMC) stock is heading for its best weekly gain since July, after the theater chain posted record third-quarter (Q3) revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and CEO Adam Aron declared on X that AMC “has recovered”—a stock attempting to claw back four years of losses. AMC Entertainment stock traded over 2% lower overnight, ahead of Thursday. The stock has gained 15% so far this week and is on track to reverse four years of losses. The rally tests whether a record quarter can change how Wall Street prices a company that spent years as a survival story. AMC still reported a nine-month GAAP net loss, and its stock trades at a valuation unlike its peers’. Aron is betting that a $10 billion-plus box office makes the old debt and dilution worries obsolete. For the better part of four years, AMC Entertainment’s story was about staying alive. This week, its CEO argued that story is over. “Today, we can finally say that AMC has recovered,” Aron posted on X after the company reported Q3 results on Wednesday. He called the quarter “a triumph” and said AMC’s biggest and best in its 106-year history. The numbers back him on growth. Q3 revenue rose 31.6% year-on-year to $1.711 billion, up from $1.300 billion last year. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 183.7% to $347.5 million, nearly triple last year’s figure. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 20.3%, more than double the 9.4% from a year ago. It was the second straight quarter in which AMC set all-time company records for both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. Analysts had expected about $1.62 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.10 a share, according to Fiscal.ai estimates cited by Stocktwits. AMC reported adjusted earnings of $0.13, against a loss of 58 cents a year ago. Operating cash flow was $176.6 million, versus a $14.9 million outflow a year ago. Free cash flow was $109.3 million, which brings the year-to-date total to $124.7 million. That is why Aron sees AMC posting positive free cash flow for all of 2026. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to $751.9 million, excluding $39.6 million in restricted cash. Attendance did the heavy lifting. Q3 attendance rose 28.3% to 74.9 million moviegoers, with international markets up 41.5% and U.S. markets up 23.3%. AMC did this with slightly fewer screens, averaging 9,177 versus 9,354 a year ago. The company also reported record revenue per patron, which Aron credited to its loyalty programs and its growing roster of premium large-format auditoriums. Aron also leaned on the balance sheet. On Oct. 5, AMC completed a $3.97 billion refinancing covering about 97% of its debt, pushing maturities out to late 2031 and 2033. During the Q3 earnings call, Aron addressed critics directly. He called any future article describing AMC as overly debt-laden “mindlessly in error.” He said “groundless fears of endless share dilution will come only from those looking in the rearview mirror.” He did not rule out new stock sales, saying AMC will “wisely utilize equity financings when it makes sense.” His argument rests on the macro backdrop. AMC now operates in a box office above $10 billion, he said, “a very different animal” from the $7 billion to $9 billion range of the past four years. Q4 looks strong so far. Aron said October’s domestic box office ran about 35% above the same month last year. The remaining slate includes The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Dune: Part Three, Avengers: Doomsday and Jumanji: Open World. Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management said in an X post that slower capital spending on data centers across the technology industry could reduce pressure on memory component prices, potentially supporting Apple's future profitability. Bernstein also increased its Apple price target to $380 from $370, citing better-than-anticipated quarterly performance and encouraging revenue guidance for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. XTB research director Kathleen Brooks also warned that increased congressional scrutiny could delay a transaction. “While Congress cannot stop a merger, they could slow it down via extra scrutiny,” she said. Gary Black, managing partner of The Future Fund, warned that an all-stock SpaceX-Tesla deal might deliver less value than bulls expect, pointing to Marvell Technology’s (MRVL) acquisition of Lumentum Holdings (LITE). “As we’ve learned (again) from $MRVL - $LITE deal, a +24% premium can quickly go negative as the acquirer’s stock is sold down,” he said on X. But the fixed exchange ratio means the offer’s dollar value falls alongside Marvell’s stock. With the deal expected to close in the first half of 2028, Black warned that Tesla investors could face a similarly lengthy wait. “A SPCX-TSLA deal given its size and complexity could take just as long,” he said earlier this week. title: MSFT Stock Surges Above $555 to New Record Highs as Midterms Lift Microsoft and Big Tech - FXLeaders
content: Microsoft stock has rallied above $555 to a new record after recovering from a decline toward $500, as strong cloud growth and improving sentiment following the U.S. midterm elections support buyers, despite growing scrutiny of infrastructure spending and future computing commitments. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) shares have staged a sharp recovery after falling toward $500, with the stock extending its gains today to break above $557 and establish a new record high. The rebound follows renewed concerns about the company’s relationship with Anthropic, rising infrastructure costs and the substantial investment required to expand its computing capacity. Improving sentiment across technology stocks following the U.S. midterm elections has provided another catalyst. Investors are reassessing the potential impact of political pressure on data-centre construction, particularly as electricity costs, grid stability and water consumption become increasingly important issues. Greater regulatory scrutiny could force hyperscalers to reconsider the pace of infrastructure expansion. Although this could create operational challenges, investors may also view more disciplined spending as positive for free cash flow, which has become a major concern across the technology sector. The removal of election uncertainty has also allowed markets to refocus on corporate earnings, economic conditions and the outlook for large technology companies. However, the implications of the election results for tariffs, fiscal negotiations and government policy remain uncertain. Microsoft’s latest quarterly results demonstrated continued strength across its core operations. Net income increased 32% year-over-year to $36.6 billion, or $4.92 per diluted share on a GAAP basis. Non-GAAP earnings reached $4.89 per share, excluding the impact of investments in OpenAI. Revenue increased to $90.6 billion from $77.6 billion a year earlier, while earnings comfortably exceeded the analyst consensus of $4.27 per share. Despite the strong performance, the market reaction highlighted a growing distinction between earnings growth and the returns generated from infrastructure investment. Investors are increasingly questioning whether Microsoft’s spending commitments can translate into sustainable profitability and sufficient cash generation. Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion, increasing 30% year-over-year, or 31% in constant currency. The performance highlights continued demand for cloud computing services and Microsoft’s ability to attract enterprise customers. Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said the company exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income and earnings per share. CEO Satya Nadella also highlighted improvements in computing capacity, customer choice, security and cost efficiency. Nevertheless, expanding cloud capacity requires substantial investment in data centres, servers, networking equipment and specialised processors. The challenge is ensuring that revenue growth keeps pace with capital expenditure rather than allowing infrastructure costs to weaken margins and free cash flow. Microsoft shares jumped above the critical $500 level as they rebounded strongly in the last 2 months which has now turned into a support zone, and climbed above $550 earlier in October but slipped toward $500 again on Monday. The price slip breached the 50 daily SMA in September which has been acting as support and we’re seeing a rebound today. The price has now pushed to a new record high above $555 area which represents both psychological and technical resistance so for now MAFT buyers gave up at this zone, revering lower. An amended filing concerning Microsoft’s relationship with Anthropic identifies at least $44.9 billion in commitments to Microsoft through June 2033, subject to contractual delivery and breach provisions. The disclosure relates to an existing arrangement amended during 2026 and highlights the scale of future computing demand. However, large commitments do not eliminate the risks associated with financing and infrastructure expansion. Smaller cloud providers could face greater pressure if borrowing costs remain elevated or customer demand fails to meet expectations. Recent warnings from Elon Musk about the sustainability of some infrastructure businesses have added to concerns about debt-funded data-centre construction. Microsoft has a stronger financial position than many smaller competitors, but it still needs to demonstrate that these commitments will generate attractive returns. Microsoft is also investing in its Maia 300 processor to improve computing efficiency and reduce dependence on external chip suppliers. The processor reportedly targets 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, while its 96-accelerator configuration is designed to deliver significantly higher rack-scale throughput than Maia 200. Custom silicon could eventually reduce computing costs and improve infrastructure efficiency. However, development, deployment and scaling require substantial investment before those benefits become fully visible. Microsoft has also reportedly discussed leasing computing capacity from SpaceX, although the status of those discussions remains unclear. Not every division is experiencing the same momentum. Microsoft’s Devices and Consumer segment generated $15.5 billion in revenue, down 3% year-over-year. Search and advertising revenue increased 12%, but Xbox content and services revenue declined 2%, while Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 22%. Regulatory pressure also remains a consideration. The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority has proposed designating Microsoft as having strategic market status in certain software markets, potentially increasing scrutiny of licensing, pricing and product bundling. Competition from Google Workspace could add further pressure as businesses reassess subscription costs and available alternatives. The move above $557 marks a significant recovery from the recent decline toward $500. Strong earnings, 30% Microsoft Cloud growth and substantial future computing demand continue to support the company’s fundamentals. However, the central question remains whether Microsoft’s infrastructure commitments and custom-chip investments can deliver sufficient returns. The latest rally suggests buyers are regaining confidence, but elevated spending, financing risks and regulatory scrutiny remain important considerations as the stock enters record territory.

title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Rises 6.7% as Big Tech Stocks Rally (Nov 4) - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - In the latest Microsoft stock news, shares of Microsoft (MSFT) rose 6.68% to close at $555.80 in the US session on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Financial media tied the gain in Microsoft stock to a broad postelection rally after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, with no company-specific news behind the move. Regular-session close on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since November 5, 2025. Indices and the 10-year Treasury yield: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. Follow MSFT's latest price on our Microsoft (MSFT) stock price today page. Microsoft opened at $543.70, well above the previous close of $520.99, and never traded back down to that level during the day. It moved between $542.30 and $559.15 and closed $13.50 above the day's low, near the top of its range. The day's high of $559.15 is also the stock's new 52-week high, and the close sits 0.60% below it and 59.16% above the 52-week low of $349.20. Trading was heavy. Volume reached 50.8 million shares, 125.78% above the average of 22.5 million shares. The gain far outpaced the broader market. The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.44% to 25,736.51, the S&P 500 added 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 3.03% to 53,356.12, which put Microsoft 5.24 percentage points ahead of the Nasdaq. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.8 basis points to 4.89%. Big tech peers moved the same way, while chip names did not. Apple (AAPL) rose 5.31% to $349.51 and Amazon (AMZN) gained 6.12% to $266.03, but Nvidia (NVDA) fell 3.17% to $200.13. Microsoft did not announce company-specific news on November 4, and the reports behind the move point to the election. According to CNBC, Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, plus key governor races in Texas and Georgia, and Microsoft jumped as five of the Magnificent Seven stocks rallied, with Apple touching an all-time high. As reported by Yahoo Finance, Microsoft hit a new record during a postelection relief rally, with the Democratic win paving the way for a divided government. The same report said oil prices fell as the outcome raised hopes for an end to the war in the Middle East. The rally did not reach every technology name. Per CNBC, names connected with data centers moved lower amid concern about potential restrictions on AI buildouts, after a Democratic governor-elect in Texas promised a moratorium, and Yahoo Finance reported that chip stocks including Nvidia also fell.
